claim: The statement that plain S3 did not break was misleading: plain S3 had a silent in-memory projection omission, while only the local-disk `Fake` transaction made hardlinked directories immediately visible.

The GC design moved from an epoch-based reclamation (EBR) core that encoded generation in the object key (`blobs/<H>/<g>`) and required a `404→LIST` degraded read path, durable per-hash floors, and Keeper-fenced `safe_epoch`, to an incarnation model that moves the resurrection marker into the object body and deletion precision into the backend token, eliminating generation from any key and removing the `404→LIST` path entirely.

A 2026-06-19 baseline determination against the pre-refactor binary found 68 unique failures in the `transactions` and `text-index` test families identically reproduced on the unrefactored binary, confirming they were pre-existing CA gaps (B182, B183) rather than regressions, so the refactor was declared regression-clean without any code change.

`CaIncarnationProofCore.tla` used Apalache 0.58.0 to verify an inductive invariant `IndInv` (19 conjuncts) for a pre-B91, token-only fragment of the GC core: base case (`Init => IndInv`) and step check (`IndInv => IndInv'`) both held, which is stronger than TLC bounded checking because the step check quantifies over all states satisfying `IndInv` at fixed bounds regardless of trace depth; the model was removed 2026-07-22 as stale and unverifiable in an environment without an Apalache binary.

`CaGcIndegRefoldCore.tla` modeled a bug (H1b) where an in-degree completion-seal cursor persisted at `foldCursor` instead of `max(foldCursor, fenceVersion)` caused a re-fold of an already-absorbed fence-window removal, driving the integer in-degree counter to -1 (`INV_INDEG_NONNEGATIVE` violated, mapping to `CORRUPTED_DATA` in C++); the design decision was that the `Seal` action must advance the persisted cursor to `fenceVersion`, not remain at `foldCursor`.

`CaGcIndegRefoldCore.tla` was removed 2026-07-22 because the shipped in-degree design no longer accumulates a non-idempotent integer delta stream: `CasBlobInDegree.cpp` computes in-degree via an idempotent two-cursor presence-set merge keyed by `(blob_hash, source_id)` where the surviving-edge count is an unsigned integer that structurally cannot go negative, so the underflow hazard the model existed to catch is now structurally impossible.

Three B167 build-watermark models (`CaResurrectLiveness.tla`, `CaBuildWatermark.tla`, `CaBuildWatermarkNum.tla`), all removed 2026-07-21, proved that resurrect liveness requires a guard blocking GC from re-condemning a freshly-owned incarnation during the non-atomic upload-to-publish span (the B167 livelock: dedup hit on a stale incarnation is deleted, the fresh re-upload is re-condemned by GC without a guard, looping forever); their safety role fully migrated into `CaBuildRootPrecommit.tla`'s precommit-first reachability mechanism, which replaced the modeled per-candidate blob-guard and condemn-time `HeartbeatGuard` that were never fully implemented.

The P9 GC 404-HEAD-storm fix's original mechanism, GcSnap::forget node-pruning, was later removed and superseded by the source-edge-set GC model (which has no persisted node registry to forget from); the ~90%-of-read-ops savings it was credited with is a historical measurement basis, not tied to a currently-existing mechanism.

codex_r6_findings.md's round-5 disposition table maps all 10 round-5 review findings against the v6 ref-chain redesign: fully resolved (later definite result after ambiguity; clean-transition sealing), resolved for safety only (REBUILD condemnation; cross-epoch removals), partially resolved (recovery snapshot authority; one enumeration/falsifiability), unresolved (namespace incarnation; current-epoch manifest bodies; catalog partial transitions/capacity), and resolved for the original mismatch only (CAS-walk controller mismatch) — each disposition cites which of the 13 new v6 findings covers the remaining gap. Overall verdict: REJECT.

External bug report Altinity/ClickHouse#2052 (orphan-manifest sweep deletes live manifests) does not reproduce on HEAD: the reporter's build was ~330 commits behind and predated commit `318291fe5e5`, which switched the orphan-manifest sweep's ownership recovery onto `recoverRefTable` (the ref-log model) rather than the older `recoverRefTableDetailed` path.

The reftable COW-map plan's self-review found the actual access-site inventory for `RefTableState::committed` was 18 sites across 5 files (verified against the tree), not the ~15 sites the spec estimated; all but one site was a drop-in change.

The full-scale P0 campaign found six O(N) cost families: GC round O(pool objects), scratch equal to full part size, replicated `OPTIMIZE` double-spill, wide-part O(columns), partitioned INSERT O(partitions), and startup O(refs).
The rev.5 five-second grace floor was measured to cause approximately 20–26 GB/hour of ref snapshot traffic per node in the cited soak.

In the measured 500-partition profile, `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::finishDelayed` commits partitions serially, the ref-ledger batch size is 1.0, and `CasRefBatchFlushes` equals `CasRefBatchedMutations` at 1026.

The S41 wide-insert baseline found CAS-on-S3 at 3.0× slower than plain S3, with 87.2% of Real time in S3 network operations, 12.6% in the HEAD-before-PUT gate, and about 77 blob PUTs per part on the wide profile.
The wide S41 CA INSERT fell from 58.41 seconds before stage 1 to 30.26 seconds after stage 1, a 48% reduction and 1.93x speedup; plain S3 remained 19.44 versus 19.05 seconds.
The S41 stage-1 workload produced 500 CA parts and 3.53 GiB of logical bytes in both runs, while the CA-vs-plain factor fell from 3.0x to 1.59x.
The wide S41 profile averaged approximately 80 blob upload fan-out tasks per part (`40,150 / 500`), explaining why intra-part fan-out exceeded the narrow-case estimate of roughly two blobs per part.
On the CA INSERT, stage 1 reduced the top thread's Real-sample share from 72.3% to 14.5%, increased distinct Real-trace threads from 3 to 33, and increased CPU-busy/wall from 0.375 to 1.075.
The CA write path remained S3-network-bound at about 87% of Real wall time after stage 1; stage 1 overlapped that network work without removing it, while the HEAD-before-PUT gate remained about 12%.
For the 500-part S41 CA leg, PUTs stayed at 119,432, while HEADs fell from 134,400 to 105,140 and GETs from 54,360 to 42,656 after stage 1.

The A1 benchmark gate kept the production-shaped `BM_FlushInstallUniqueOwner` within baseline: at N=100,000 it measured 13,355 ns before A1 and 12,428 ns after A1, while the shared-base `BM_FlushInstall` measured 21,208,894 ns after A1.
The A1 benchmark's `BM_ScratchCopy` remained O(1) at about 58 ns after the restructure, and `BM_ApplyRefLogTxn` remained within measurement noise at 770–831 ns versus 800–864 ns baseline.
The upstream patch inventory counts 12 logical class-A hunks, 67 class-B hunks, and 3 class-C hunks.

The `RefTableState` closed-class experiments round's success criterion (Task 8 final gate) is: after a 20-minute soak, the hottest CAS-attributed CPU stack family in the `trace_log` profile must be blob hashing, and every other CAS-attributed family must be at most one third of blob hashing's sample count; a miss turns the residual hotspot into a new experiment row rather than closing the round.
Mutable integer blob refcounts were rejected in favor of an idempotent source-edge set folded from append-only +/- journal records.
The gc/registry namespace registry was removed because it grew monotonically, made GC cost proportional to namespaces ever created times root_shards, and did not reclaim empty shards.
Reading every run block with a separate ranged GET was rejected because a full 8 GB run would require about 32,000 requests per shard.
Persisting integer refcounts and folding `prior_count + Σ ±1` was rejected because a refolded removal can underflow the count and wedge GC with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
A separate intermediate tree-layer object was rejected because it added key-space and GC edge complexity without benefit beyond recursive subtrees and identity decoupling.

The raw immutable-body freshness-meta design with terminal tombstones was rejected because it introduced writer–GC waiting and liveness coupling; the current design keeps one hash key with an in-body incarnation tag and exact-token body deletion.
Per-incarnation blob keys such as `blobs/xx/<hash>.<incarnation>` were rejected because they require `404 → LIST` reads and propagate incarnation into manifests and parents.
An EBR or epoch GC core never existed in C++; EBR appears only in TLA+ and design documents, while the C++ path went directly from PoC reachability to the `Cas::Store` token model.
The P9 `GcSnap::forget` cascade was short-lived: `GcSnap::forget` and `GForget` were added by `3243c6aec96` and `03e11643db3`, then the `CasGcSnap` unit was deleted by `3526407f1b1` ten days later.
Comparing hot snapshots through bare `checksums.txt` equality or filesystem inode witnesses was rejected; the CAS-native identity primitive is streaming re-hashing and pool-side deduplication.

The CAS design rejects a Merkle `treeId` layer, EBR or epoch-based GC, integer refcounts, `gc/registry` as discovery authority, endpoint-plus-prefix pool matching, and CAS-specific fields in `ReplicatedMergeTreePartHeader`.

Writer deregistration at `dropNamespace` was rejected because removal events carry the blob `-1` edges and removing the namespace from discovery before GC folds them could cause phantom in-degree leaks.
GC deregistration based on an empty settled namespace was rejected because a freshly created live table with no inserts is indistinguishable from a dropped table by emptiness alone.
Copy-forward rejects recreating from writer-local files because a CA part's files are the pool blobs and no independent source exists on the move path.
A same-`ManifestId` owner-move rename with Δ=0 was rejected because cross-shard moves would create two-owner or zero-owner windows that the source-edge set model cannot represent.
The design rejects one ranged GET per block for full scans because an 8 GB run would require approximately 32,000 requests per shard per pass; ranged block GETs remain only for `seek`.

The cache-over-CA design rejects making the generic cache wrapper impersonate CA concrete types and rejects peeling wrappers at every dynamic-cast site; direct CA metadata reuse has the smaller blast radius.
`ManifestExpand`, `ManifestRetire`, and `ManifestStrip` are obsolete dead enum entries from the removed Merkle layer and must be deleted rather than implemented.

The rejected trust-until-invalidated generation-counter design would have depended on discovering every mutation site and a root-lease argument that does not cover pool-global shadow namespaces; validate-on-hit was chosen instead.

Serving a retained view for `ForceFresh` after only a matching ref resolve was rejected because ref currency does not prove manifest-body existence; `ForceFresh` therefore always performs the mandatory `HEAD` through `readManifestShared`.

A four-value `Freshness` enum was rejected because the mutable-read versus write-evidence distinction is carried by the method: mutable reads call `resolve`, while write-evidence reads call `getView(ForceFresh)`.
Materialized file and directory indexes were rejected because decoder-enforced canonical order makes binary search over the shared decode simpler and lighter.

Relocating `shard_decode_cache` and `dedup_cache` into a `CasCacheState` was rejected as unnecessary verified-machinery movement with regression risk; the memory goal is met by byte-bounding `manifest_cache` in Phase 5.
Comparing whole PartManifest objects is rejected because ref, root_namespace_id, and payload_digest legitimately differ between source and destination manifests.
The raw-body v1 cut was rejected because dropping the in-body incarnation tag fixed the body etag to content and removed the protection that makes exact-token deletion miss a resurrected body.
The v2 terminal-tombstone design was superseded because it couples writer progress to GC and is unnecessary when the body tag changes the etag on resurrection.
Per-incarnation body keys were rejected because they require generation resolution by LIST, propagate incarnation into manifests, and break the pure-content/FUSE-ready design.
Retired-in-snapshot does not change round pacing or the one-round graduation gap, because that gap is the racing-writer edge-surfacing window under EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE.
Moving `clearSparedMeta` after the winning `gc/state` CAS is insufficient because an older leader can execute a stale pre-CAS `deleteExact` after a newer leader adopts a spare and clears the meta.
Settlement is not partitioned by algorithm: mixed rows remain in the same `gc_shards` runs, and schemas 1 and 2 plus digest-only settlement helpers are deleted without compatibility shims.
Mixed-algorithm pools do not rehash existing blobs, perform cross-algorithm deduplication, support per-table or per-insert algorithm selection, or remove algorithms from `algos_used`.
The recommended default layout includes the `ch128` path segment rather than retaining the legacy no-segment cityHash128 layout, because CA has no persisted-data compatibility requirement.
Phase 1 rejects a global ref-sequence watermark because lexical scan order differs from sequence order across tables and a global watermark could mark unseen concurrent appends as folded.
The optional memory fast path is a separable optimization: small S3-mode blobs may be buffered in memory and written with `putIfAbsentStream`, while large blobs use S3 staging and conditional copy.
The late-predecessor TLA+ configuration intentionally retains an expected-fail counterexample in which an old-epoch log materializes after a successor scan and violates complete-recovery safety.
The token-diff `Skip` machinery and `listTokens` capability were removed because ref GC now detects changes from logs above each per-table cursor, and `listTokens` has no production callers at HEAD.

Timeout control reduces but does not eliminate late-predecessor S3 completion; Keeper-based commit or another cross-object fencing mechanism remains a separate possible solution for strict cross-epoch authority.
The single-value `ObjectKind` enum is deliberately retained because it is threaded through about 100 consumers and removing it would be a refactor rather than clean subtraction.
`CasEvent::round` is not removed because it is a live serialized field surfaced as `system.content_addressed_log.round`, despite the earlier premise that it was always zero.

The absence-means-Clean blob-meta lever was abandoned on 2026-07-14 and will not be revived because clearing the GC tombstone reopened a data-loss hole; the optimization round ships §§1–4 and §6 without §5.

The design rejected a decommission-intent marker executed by `GC` because it would require `GC` to invent ref transitions, and rejected raw prefix deletion followed by mandatory `ca-gc-rebuild` because it would break in-degree accounting until an O(universe) rebuild; the chosen design makes the command a temporary writer using existing writer machinery.
The rev.5 `snapshot_min_log_age_ms` grace window could leave a late predecessor log visible to cold folds while permanently absent from the writer's state.
The proposal's recovery-seal-at-listed-maximum rule was later corrected to the dead-epoch upper-bound rule because an unresolved predecessor ID can exceed the greatest listed ID.
The abandoned §5 plan proposed making blob meta a pure tombstone where absent meta means Clean, with fresh-body-first resurrect and spare tombstone clearing.
The read-only replica design rejects reader-to-writer promotion, an `H_max` snapshot-age cap, per-blob read pins, and making the reader a full pool member as scope for this design.

Owner-transition bindings use flat `o` and `n` key prefixes rather than nested JSON objects because the flat `JsonObjectReader` has no array or nesting support and extending it would increase the blast radius.

`CasRecordStreamFormat` and the fixed-offset blob-envelope codec are not reused for part manifests because the former is source-edge-specific and the latter supports only one raw payload rather than multiple banner segments.

Transport-level seals such as sender ACKs, response suffixes, HTTP trailers, and full-duplex reverse channels were rejected because Poco interserver transport is half-duplex and response-side data cannot provide a reverse acknowledgement or backpressure.

A CA-specific disk `precommit` phase is rejected because the relevant `Keeper`/disk ordering is general to real disk transactions, while a CA-only phase would add an extra visibility boundary and upstream conflict surface without solving the general problem.

The design rejects deferred delete intents, disk-queue replay before commit, replay in a new `precommit`, reuse of `IDataPartStorage::precommitTransaction`, `publishStagedData`, publication from `moveDirectory`, and a CA-specific transaction subclass or split base.

Preserving staged merged parts or implementing resume-upload is explicitly out of scope because content-addressed blob deduplication bounds recompute cost once lease renewal stops over-fencing and merge backoff engages.

The proposed `CasBlobUploader` split was descoped because `putBlob`, `observeAndAdmit`, and `uploadFromSource` form one mutually recursive writer-protocol lane whose decision state is coupled to byte delivery and shared mid-flight state.

The one-pipeline design adds no `IDiskTransaction::precommit`, `IMetadataTransaction::precommit`, or `IDataPartStorage::publishStagedData`, and does not change `IDataPartStorage::precommitTransaction` or the Replicated `Keeper` call sequence.
`freeze` cannot provide the MOVE-to-CA copy primitive because its transactional `Backup()` path uses same-disk `transaction->copyFile`, which throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for cross-disk CA copies.

The `freeze` transaction seam cannot be reused for cross-disk MOVE because `DiskObjectStorageTransaction::copyFile` calls `generateObjectKeyForPath`, which throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on CA, while generic disk copy primitives use autocommit writes.

Deferring `clonePart`'s commit into the swap is rejected because `clonePart` must commit before `create(initialize=true)` reads the part back, and changing that contract would enlarge the generic mover surface.

The persistent ordered-tree approach, an `absl::btree_map` base, and changes to `precommits` are out of scope for the COW-map cut; commit-path tracing and microbenchmark evidence are separate follow-up work.
A persistent immutable ordered tree is deferred, `absl::btree_map` is optional follow-up work, and `precommits` remains unchanged.

Verify-on-dedup remains out of scope as the primary fix because it adds a read to every dedup hit and does not close merge-path ordering windows; CA-only publish-at-rename and a new `IDiskTransaction::precommit` phase were also rejected.
T5 intentionally adds no new un-decommission CLI flag; manual clearing of `retired_at_ms` is the only revival path in this fix.

The benchmark's `BM_MemcpyTxnBytes` floor was 30.7 ns, making the implemented 333 ns encoder about 10.8× the floor rather than the planned ≤3× target; the target was rejected as physically unreachable because a correct encoder must still validate, format numbers, escape JSON, and allocate its buffer.

The incremental-budget design rejects a conservative over-estimate because byte-exactness is provable, rejects caching full encoded strings because it would retain two full strings and require line splicing, and rejects reducing `admits()` frequency because it changes per-operation validation granularity.

The E4 flat-vector `RefCowMap` base was reverted because only `BM_Materialize` met the two-times target at N=100,000 while `BM_MergedIteration` improved by at most 1.28 times and `BM_SnapshotEncode` stayed within noise.
The landed Dormant/UNMOUNT lifecycle is unsound because its benign-absent behavior can silently skip reclaim and make ATTACH load an empty table when data may still exist.

Lazy `ensureMounted()` from `store()` is rejected because it inverts the `lifecycle_mutex → gc_scheduler_mutex → pointer_mutex` lock order and can deadlock; a benign probe also cannot distinguish table binding from a sweep.

The original phased design's byte-estimate admission was rejected because undercounting could make whole-batch `checkBudget` throw; v2 replaces it with exact operation-count admission and a per-operation size cap.
The retention-pin design was rejected because it would add a pool-global GC overlay, union folding, removal deferral, and owner-liveness machinery to the most safety-critical component.

The reserved-precommit design was abandoned because it caused state-model sprawl, let a foreign writer bypass `stageManifest` and `adoptEvidence` discipline, and mismatched the `tmp-fetch_<part>` contract.
The superseded branch was intentionally out of scope in the first proposal, but v2 later classifies it as normal fencing because a different epoch indicates a distinct remount incarnation.

Adopt-and-continue of the observed mount token was rejected because it violated the contract that `onRenewMismatch` must throw and would require proof that an unwitnessed body is safe to adopt; fence plus self-remount already exists and is exercised.
The v2 design explicitly leaves body-nonce rescue, coherent-read machinery, resolve-on-ambiguity, and changes to the mount-lease format out of scope; the safety mechanism is fence plus remount.

`Pool::openForDecommission` already provides a reversible alternative by reading the existing owner uuid and impersonating it, preserving pool identity while allowing a WRITE mount; its tradeoff is that two processes present the same owner uuid and rely on the mount lease to serialize them.

Banning a database engine or restricting generation tokens to shadow paths was rejected because it would break supported same-name reuse and replicated-database recovery while leaving other rebirth routes unprotected.

Serial exact `GET N+1` until 404 was rejected because every probe costs a full S3 round trip, concurrent writing makes the stop unstable, and 404 proves object absence rather than acknowledged-history completeness.

Recovery from a complete stream LIST was rejected because completeness is the premise under test; recovery performs zero stream LIST calls and uses enumeration only for leak-only GC/janitor discovery.

The ref-layer `materialization_grace` wait is expected to be deleted because arithmetic recovery no longer trusts listings for completeness and the in-band seal fences late stragglers deterministically; the setting must not remain parsed but inert.

This series does not move namespace files into the ref log, add folder-state manifests or a `_raw_files` object family, change `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog`, merge `Poisoned` into wedge, refactor `RefApplyState`, or remove the plain-object component.

Adding `INVALID_STATE` to `isRetryableException` was rejected because it would reclassify 18 sites, including eight terminal CA sites and eight non-CA sites; recoding the three selected transient sites to `NETWORK_ERROR` fixes the required behavior with zero unintended reclassifications.

The relink protocol deliberately sends no `ETag`, `If-None-Match`, `If-Modified-Since`, or `If-Match`; standard conditional vocabulary was rejected because an intermediary could evaluate it and synthesize a response, including a forged 304, instead of consulting the sender.

The per-ref `MutationScope` index was rejected as a pre-ship stopgap because it adds protocol complexity to narrow the lane terms and would undermine the surface-deletion goal; a refusal is retry-later and therefore an availability cost rather than a correctness hazard.

The recovery token bucket, cache-class segmentation, and per-peer fairness machinery were rejected as overengineering; only the per-recovery work cap and hard-coded global concurrency limit remain, with cold-confirm share as the revisit tripwire.

Receiver-pays verification by directly recovering the sender's ref state was rejected because each verification would perform LIST plus replay and would inherit the listing-trust problems that the v9 chain is intended to remove.

The 304/503 response-status encoding was rejected: `assertResponseIsOk` accepts only 200, 201, 202, 206 and redirects, so 304 and 503 would arrive as exceptions and require shared HTTP-client changes; the protocol keeps tri-state values in explicit headers on 200 responses.

Having the receiver verify sender ref state directly from the pool was rejected because although it makes the beneficiary pay and removes the DoS class, it performs LIST plus replay per confirm and inherits LIST-trust questions.

A bounded re-`LIST` or retry triggered by an out-of-order key cannot replace catalog authority because finite scans can agree while omitting an entire namespace and therefore produce no retry trigger.
Permanent exact-`RootNamespace` non-reuse would avoid generation-based aliasing only by refusing supported exact-name reuse workflows, including shadow names and explicit UUID replay.
Deleting a catalog entry immediately after folding the terminal record permits multiple cleanup items for repeated lives of one name and breaks the fold-seal reservation bound.
A mount-time one-shot synthetic LIST probe cannot certify a backend because it can pass on RustFS even though a rare load- and timing-dependent violation later occurs.

The writer-GC simplification review rejected both unchanged-round promote HEAD skipping and per-commit pinned-round acknowledgements as unnecessary variants after adopting the `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` design; the durable precommit edge plus two-phase delete recheck remains the load-bearing safety mechanism.

Raw appending of canonical ref names was rejected because `checkCanonicalRefName` does not reject quotes, control bytes, or U+2028/U+2029; only the fixed vocabulary words `owner` and `tombstone` were proven safe for raw append.
The intermediate grace-based GC designs were intentionally superseded by the incarnation, pin, lease, and fence model; this is treated as intended design history rather than lost durable content.

The four `EnableTokenDiff = TRUE` configurations `stage5_tokendiff`, `sab_skipchangedshard`, `sab_skipparksdeadprecommit`, and `fix_skipparksdeadprecommit` were retired because no production seam legitimately consumes a LIST-derived token as authority to skip the fold read.
`INV_RECONCILE_SAFE_BRIEF` is not a valid gate because its proposed state formula rejects the legitimate transient state where a creator fence is terminal before `_ckpt` creation.

The retired `_sab_fix_ckptwitness` and `_witness_corruptgap` obligations are unconstructible because `_ckpt.committed_through`, rather than `_ckpt.checkpoint` or a higher `LIST` witness, is now the exact bound and every missing key at or below it creates a hold.
Gate 0 is only an availability filter and authorizes nothing; safety belongs to gate 1, so modeling gate 0 would create a false impression of two independent safety sources.
The original epoch-based reclamation GC with a global epoch and per-writer pins was superseded by the incarnation-token design because no epoch machinery exists in the shipped code.
Per-incarnation body keys were rejected because they reintroduce incarnation into keys and manifests, require a 404-then-`LIST` read path, and break pure-content manifests.
A meta-absence-means-clean tombstone variant was rejected because clearing a condemned marker in place is unsafe under the add-only freshness-meta proof and no such code landed.
The per-candidate minimum-active-build watermark mechanism was replaced by precommit-first reachability; the surviving requirement is that build sequence numbers come from a monotone counter.
The Merkle `treeId` tree layer was rejected because it added complexity without a correctness benefit; tree objects are manifest-internal.
The EBR GC core was rejected because per-object epoch state did not scale; GC uses incarnation-token identity instead.
Integer in-degree refcounting was rejected because non-atomic folding under concurrent leaders could undercount; the source-edge set replaced it.
V1 rejects a generic folder-view API in `IMetadataStorage` because it would broaden the disk API, increase fork conflicts, and still not express CAS-specific freshness rules.
`Cas::Store` must not own part-folder cache policy because that would mix protocol, metadata filesystem semantics, and operational tuning.
V1 rejects generic path-result caching because the workload is specifically a part/projection folder load window and arbitrary path invalidation would complicate mutable files.
The architecture analysis does not recommend merging `CasPoolMeta` and `CasRootsRegistry` codecs because their create-once and mutable-CAS lifecycles differ.
v2 rejects ClickHouse CompressedWriteBuffer for CAS bodies and chooses plain single-frame zstd so the protocol remains portable outside ClickHouse
v2 rejects an all-protobuf design because unbounded GC data would lose bounded-memory streaming and ranged seek
v2 rejects FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto because CAS metadata is small and object-storage network latency dominates parsing, while the dependencies add no needed portability
v3 rejects v2's framed protobuf design because it keeps the control plane behind bespoke tooling and adds integrity guards whose failures change no decision
v3 rejects Avro and Parquet for cas_run because seek is dead in production, they add dependencies, and their container or row-group machinery does not fit two-hash marker records
v3 rejects keeping per-block CRC and footer in cas_run because the seal checksum covers the whole file that all consumers actually read

CAS mechanisms are rejected when they require Keeper for correctness, scale Keeper or S3 work with data volume, let a stuck writer stall pool-wide reclamation, can accelerate deletion past safety gates, or couple generic `ReplicatedMergeTree` surfaces to the CA disk implementation.

Per-incarnation body keys such as `blobs/xx/<hash>.<incarnation>` were rejected because they recreate the generation-in-key race, force `404 → LIST`, and leak incarnation into pure-content manifest identity.
The `CasNamespaceFileDiskProfile.SteadyStateFileOperationsTouchNoCatalogRefBlobOrManifestKey` test does not exercise the `listNamespaceFiles` arm; direct list-arm coverage is provided separately.

SensitivityCheckOrderingComparisonDiscriminates is not a valid sensitivity check because EXPECT_FALSE(*body_index > *ckpt_index) duplicates the scenario and is weaker than test 1's EXPECT_LT(*body_index, *ckpt_index); the recorded mutation run is the meaningful evidence.
The historical alternative of widening probe A was rejected; probe A is deleted outright rather than demoted or retained as a sampling mechanism.

The ordinary `clickhouse-disks write` verb currently does not reach `blobUploadPool()` because plain files use `CaInlineWriteBuffer` and part-shaped autocommit writes are `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; pool initialization there is defense-in-depth for other or future non-autocommit paths.
The `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkAlterPartitionIsPossible` override that only delegates to the virtual base adds no behavior and should be deleted together with its header declaration.

A Merkle treeId tree layer (content-addressed trees/<T> objects forming a Merkle DAG of immutable folders, with tree hashes carrying child_gen inside the tree identity) was rejected: child_gen inside tree identity forced ancestor rebuilds whenever a blob's generation floor moved, the 404->LIST degraded read path for generation resolution added latency and complexity, and the generation-in-key model required durable per-hash floors, epochs, per-build pins, quiescence machinery, and Keeper as a required component. It was replaced by the incarnation-token design; the trees/ key prefix and ObjectKind::Tree were removed entirely (2026-07-03) -- ObjectKind now has only Blob.

An EBR (Epoch-Based Reclamation) GC core -- writers holding a pin epoch (an ephemeral Keeper node), GC advancing through safe_epoch/commit_epoch/birth_epoch and waiting for quiescence, with generations on blob keys (blobs/<H>/<g>) as the ABA guard -- was rejected because a stuck or wedged writer held down safe_epoch and stalled reclamation of all dropped parts across all writers, Keeper was required for correctness, and a long-running INSERT could delay GC for its entire duration. It was replaced by the incarnation-token design, where regular GC candidates are restricted to journal-known nodes so fresh uploads are structurally invisible and can never be candidates, and a wedged writer has no pin to hold down.

CasEvent::round was NOT removed despite the original stabilization spec calling it a dead always-0 field with 5 write sites; at HEAD it has 20 write sites, is copied into ContentAddressedLogElement::round, and is a live serialized system.content_addressed_log.round column, so deleting it would be a user-visible schema change.

The single-value ObjectKind enum was NOT removed (spec item D1f) despite being a single-valued enum: it is threaded as the parameter/field type of observeAndAdmit, uploadFromSource, decodeEnvelopeHeader, magicFor, retiredLogicalSize, EnvelopeHeader::kind, RetiredEntry::kind, the CasGcOutcomes codec, and Fsck/GcObserved, with ~100 consumers; removing it is a refactor, not a subtraction.

Whole-object copy-on-write for `RefTableState::committed` via `src/Common/COW.h` (clone the whole map on any write) was rejected as "approach C" because trial copies during a flush always write, so it gives no gain over the naive full-map copy.

Proposed fix: add tryLogCurrentException (CachedPartFolderAccess.cpp).

`ObjectStorageBackend::list` in `EmulatedSingleProcess` mode fills `lk.token` from `child->metadata->etag` (`CasObjectStorageBackend.cpp:781-783`) while emulated `head`/`get`/`putOverwrite`/`deleteExact` all use `emuObserveToken`; a consumer that reuses `listed.token` for `deleteExact` (the orphan-manifest sweep, `CasOrphanManifestSweep.cpp:300`) can get a token mismatch and leave GC debris undeleted in that test-only mode. Production `Native` S3 is unaffected because both `list` and `head` return the real S3 ETag.

GC registered defect R2: `PartWriteTxn`'s destructor unconditionally retired its build sequence, advancing the GC floor while the precommit grant's outcome was still uncertain, making an uncertain owner grant look dead; the fix is a duty queue with the failure direction inverted (settle then retire then pop), where any throw retains the duty and a full queue pins the floor, since an advanced floor is an irreversible authorization while a pinned one only costs latency.

The rev.8 disk-lifecycle whole-increment final review found two Important pre-release defects, both TOCTOU races around the `gc_scheduler_mutex`: (I-1) a manual `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC RUN` admitted while the pool was `Live` could queue behind FORGET's `gc_scheduler_mutex` and, once granted, resume and run a full GC round against a since-decommissioned (`Vanished`) pool; (I-2) `runGcRebuildNow` did not take `gc_scheduler_mutex` at all, making a GC rebuild invisible to FORGET and able to durably write after FORGET believed all GC threads were stopped. Both were fixed with a lock-then-gate pattern (matching `gcStart`) plus RED-demo regression tests.

A pre-release v3 data-loss hole was found while modeling the deposed-leader path in TLA+: a deposed GC leader's pre-CAS `clearSparedMeta` call leaves stray-Clean freshness metadata over a `delete_pending` blob; a writer can then reuse the condemned blob's exact token, and the pending exact-token redelete for that token deletes the live reuse, violating `INV_NO_LOSS`. The fix made GC freshness metadata add-only (never `Condemned`->`Clean` on a spare leader; only a writer holding a fresh incarnation token may publish `Clean`), verified by a TLA+ witness plus 5 sabotage configurations including a `post_adoption_clear` case that produces an authentic 16-state 2-leader counterexample against the naive fix.

A post-soak leak-rca investigation verdict: the T8v2 soak's 169,837 vs 79 reachable/unreachable checkpoint reading was NOT a leak but an AwaitingGc fold backlog mid-churn that drained to 14 by run end; the real bug was the tripwire formula, fixed by moving the strict check to final-converge (mid-run track-only).

Opt-round §4 review Minor 2 (pre-existing, not introduced by the round): `CasBlobAdoptTrusted` increment and the manifest-trust audit-emit sit inside promote's `appendRefOps` closure, which `mutateShard` may re-invoke on a CAS retry, causing a possible counter over-count or duplicate manifest-trust event under contention; no correctness impact, same site/class as the older copy-forward increment.

A production regression where a stateless test (`05008`) went red was traced to `UniversePolicy::kDefault == StageA_Suppressed`, which suppresses destructive GC on every production round; the introducing commit swept 20+ gtest files and touched zero files under `tests/queries/`, so its stateless-test blast radius was invisible to its own test run.

A persistent shard clamp halts all GC reclamation pool-wide (G-N1): GC's fail-closed uncertainty handling means one unresolved anomaly stops reclamation everywhere, not just for the affected shard; the recommended fix keeps the fail-closed behavior but adds observability and an operator escape (clamp age, clamped key/shard, alerting, documented fsck/rebuild path), with scoped suppression deferred as a later option.

In the CA transient-classifier audit, `CasBlobInDegree.cpp:289` versus `pruneSupersededGenerations` (`CasGc.cpp:3217`, called from `:802`) has a plausible residual window where a deposed leader mid-read of a superseded generation could see benign absence misreported as `CORRUPTED_DATA`; it is GC-plane and contained, but worth confirming impossible.

P3-B1 root cause was a pre-existing GC lease/fold livelock, not a Phase-3 regression: a large deletion pipeline makes each fold take minutes, the GC lease expires mid-fold, the other node legitimately adopts leadership, the first node's round CAS then aborts (`gc/state moved`) after its pre-CAS redeletes already executed, the pipeline never shrinks, and the cycle repeats as sustained dual-leader round fights; safety held throughout (dangling=0, unaccounted=0).

The C1(b) fix was not addressed as originally stated: the frontier-completion predicate is byte-identical and the commit only changed the numerator's source; the equivalent guarantee holds only as an implicit invariant across three separate sites rather than the single explicit predicate that was requested, and this gap is exactly what NEW-1's incarnation-mismatch route exploits.

D4 (structural duplication): delete-outcome classification (Deleted/NotFound/TokenMismatch/marker) is reimplemented with local accounting across GC's R3 phase, manifest cleanup, `cleanupRefObjects`, `runNamespaceCleanupPasses`, the orphan sweep, and the staging sweeper — same tolerated-outcome set, per-site counters/events, a semantic-drift risk though not yet a bug.
D5 (structural duplication): manual LIST/cursor pagination loops are independently implemented in GC fold, `changedShardCount`, the orphan sweep, fsck, `listMounts`, and `recoverRefTable`.

D6: GC (LIST `cas/refs/`), fsck (refs plus raw-listing diff), the orphan sweep (manifest paging plus watermark), and the frontend's `listNamespaces` (refs union roots) each discover the namespace/universe differently because each answers a different question (live set vs physical set vs eligibility); the definitions are not centrally owned, so fsck, GC, and the sweep can disagree — each grew independently in a different GC era.

Risk register #7 (Medium, confidence Med): `CasGc.cpp`'s `suppress_destructive` flag is computed twice from the same mutable `report.anomalies` (at `:635` and `:1149`), with consistency between the two computations implicit rather than enforced; a future edit could make fold suppress deletes while the round itself doesn't (or vice versa), an over-delete class. Suggested action: compute it once in `fold` and thread it through `FoldResult`.

Risk register #10 (Medium, confirmed): `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:203,316` lazily creates `gc_scheduler` without a mutex; two concurrent `SYSTEM ... GC` statements could race the `make_unique` call, producing a torn scheduler pointer if not otherwise serialized upstream. Suggested action: confirm interpreter serialization, or add a mutex.

Under the RemovalReady proposal, a corrupt/unvalidatable terminal removal record leaves the cleanup item permanently `Pending` (fail-closed) so the name is never recreatable until FORCE REBUILD or decommission — a deliberate posture flip from the old design's leak-only cleanup-failure behavior, but the review flags it as an unowned posture change needing an explicit unwedge path and operator-visible surfacing.
High #1 was a GC regression where retire/preview hardcoded shard 0, causing shard-1..N blobs to leak; fixed in commit `5f5fa5f7906`.

CLAMP-SUPPRESSION was the 2026-07-03 night-soak bug where 31 dangling objects accumulated because a clamped fold cursor suppressed graduations and deletes pool-wide even though only one table was lagging.
M1 requires the cross-round fold cursor to survive trim, otherwise a double-count over-pin/leak occurs.

Blocking issue: cursor pruning is not monotone across crash-resume — if the process stops after the pruned seal is durable but before `_ckpt`/entry deletion, the catalog still shows `Removing`, and a later GC round adds every `Live`/`Removing` entry back to `walk_targets` and writes a cursor for it, reintroducing the pruned cursor; the resumed removal driver then has no safe-and-live choice between trusting the historical pruned seal or waiting on the current seal indefinitely.

The rewritten Task 5's claim that stale-resume re-derivation is unconstructible contradicts both the spec's mandated capture-at-deposition rule and the existing TLA+ model `CaRefNsCleanupStaleLeaderCore.tla`, which constructs the exact interleaving (capture, stall, removal retires and deletes the entry, name is reborn, stale leader resumes and re-derives, targeting the live incarnation and violating `NoLiveDataDeleted`).

`clearSparedMeta` (`Core/CasGc.cpp:106-113`) clears a blob's freshness meta from Condemned to Clean when a GC round spares it, scheduled on the spare verdict and completed BEFORE the round's single `gc/state` CAS; a GC leader that runs it and then loses the CAS leaves a durable stray-Clean meta over a blob still `delete_pending` in the durably-adopted run. Stray-Clean is the unsafe direction (unlike stray-Condemned, which only costs an unnecessary resurrect) because it defeats the writer's freshness gate, letting a writer reuse the exact condemned incarnation token; a later pending exact-token redelete then deletes the live reused incarnation.

A regular GC round folds ref logs into source-edge in-degree runs, performs pre-CAS exact-token deletes of prior delete_pending entries, commits the round with one gc/state CAS, and performs cleanup after that CAS.
Physical deletion requires a durable retire entry, fences at all root shards, a fold-through-fence zero-reachability recheck, and the exact observed token (INV-NO-LOSS).
GC is leader-paced and one-pass: a stale leader may duplicate work but cannot roll back or mis-delete because operations are idempotent, monotone, or exact-token guarded.
A condemned blob has zero in-degree, an exact incarnation token observed by GC, a kCondemned sentinel row with source_id = 0, and Condemned per-blob metadata while its body may still exist.
A condemned entry becomes delete_pending only after surviving one full GC round and is deleted by the next pass with its exact token.
The GC fold uses a three-cursor streaming merge of prior edges, kCondemned rows, and current deltas, emitting at most one condemned sentinel per blob.
A crashed GC pass leaves only unadopted attempt-scoped artifacts; there is no crash-resume step, and later pruning reclaims those artifacts.
The fold barrier treats a create-precommit as non-activating until its manifest body is present; once present, manifest expansion contributes the activating +1 blob edges.
The GC subsystem is the only component authorized to delete content-addressed objects.
A follower may steal the GC lease only after observing the incumbent `(owner, seq)` unchanged across the observation window and seeing no advancing heartbeat pulse.
If `gc/hb` is absent or belongs to a different owner, the lease protocol falls back to observing `gc/state.seq`.
The authoritative pool-wide GC shard count is persisted in generation-8 `_pool_meta`; `gc/state.gc_shards` mirrors it after GC state exists.
GC discovery enumerates the live root-shard universe with `LIST(cas/refs/)`, and this LIST sweep is the only universe-proportional operation in a regular round.
A GC fold processes only the root-shard journal window `(folded_cursor, current_shard_version]`.
GC must not advance a fold cursor past a live precommit whose manifest body is absent or fails `RefMatchesBody` or `ManifestNamespaceMatches` validation.
Attempt-scoped GC artifacts are written under `gc/gen/<G_f>/attempt/<a>/` before adoption, and an unadopted attempt is invisible to readers.
The single `gc/state` CAS atomically publishes the adopted generation and attempt, folded cursors, retired references, round, and prune cursor.
When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the fold carries the parent generation's `RunRef` without run I/O; zero run I/O requires both the delta bucket and retired state to be empty.
The persisted in-degree authority is the set of active source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, with edge IDs computed by `sourceEdgeId(ManifestId, path)`.
`in_degree(blob)` is computed as the cardinality of its active source-edge set during a round and is not persisted as a separate counter.
Only blobs with an explicit zero-transition marker in the current generation are GC candidates; a blob never observed as a reference target is not a candidate.
If a blob is already absent at condemnation time, GC records no candidate and never fabricates a delete token from a 404.
Physical deletion is two-phase: a floor-eligible entry is first published as `delete_pending`, and `deleteExact` runs only for an entry pending in the previous published list.
Generation pruning skips generations still referenced by the adopted seal, while a later parent-reference hand-off deletes the entire superseded generation prefix after the CAS.
A round uses `a = lease.seq` as its attempt identifier, so competing leaders write to distinct attempt prefixes and only the lease-token `gc/state` CAS can adopt one attempt.
Patch manifests are first-class reachability roots and keep both their own delta blobs and referenced base-part blobs alive while active.
For a fixed namespace and shard, every recreated root shard has a strictly greater `incarnation`, and fold cursors are keyed by `(ns, shard, incarnation)`.

`dropNamespace` appends a tombstone as its last journal event, and GC may reclaim the shard object only after the tombstone and all prior journal events are folded; a token change from a revive prevents deletion.

`putDeterministicArtifact(Backend&, key, bytes)` is limited to GC-internal deterministic artifacts, and a pre-existing key is adopted only when its bytes are equal; divergent bytes cause `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
`supportsListTokens()` is true only when LIST returns per-key incarnation tokens; without it GC must GET every root-shard body.
`gc-snap` remains a versioned binary-plus-zstd GC-internal format rather than being converted to protobuf.
The default test fixture uses one root shard, `gc_trim_min_events=0`, and `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds=8`.
The integration test `test_cas_gc_sharded` exercises disjoint-shard GC with `gc_shards=2` and `blobShard = high64(hash) % 2`.
`CaGcLeaseCore.tla` proves atomic lease-steal isolation and no false steal of an alive mid-round leader when the advisory heartbeat is enabled.

The incarnation registry-removal model proves that a durable per-shard never-reused incarnation and a newborn shard self-floor at the current GC round are both required; neither coordinate alone suffices.
The shard-incarnation model requires reclaim to wait until the shard journal, including its tombstone, is fully folded.
The live GC-round graduation predicate is `condemn_round < current_round`, with `suppress_destructive` independently blocking graduation on a clamped pass.
`CaGcRoundDeferCore.tla` permits a non-destructive round to defer rebuilding the in-degree snapshot, but a due graduation must force-fold before deleting and deferral must be bounded.
The orphan sweep must skip a committed manifest body with a pending unsealed removal because the removal fold still needs the body to emit its decrement.
A disaster-recovery rebuild starts with an empty retired list, over-protects until the normal condemnation pipeline catches up, and mints its round above every surviving mount acknowledgement.
The current regular GC round has request complexity O(delta) plus O(servers) and one `LIST` sweep, without an O(universe) GET or PUT phase.
If a listed shard token matches the sealed folded token, GC skips the shard body `GET`; clamped-coverage shards are never skipped.
A newly condemned candidate receives one `HEAD` to capture its exact token, while an already-condemned entry is re-verified from the fold and is not re-HEADed.
Physical deletion is two-phase: condemnation is published first, then `delete_pending` is published, and the physical delete follows on a later round.
Snapshot-run consumers use one `HEAD`, one ranged tail `GET`, and one streaming body `GET`; a large footer may add one exact-footer ranged `GET`.
Snapshot-run streaming uses O(block) resident memory with a maximum current block size of 1 MiB, independent of run size.
A fully idle GC round with no journal changes and no retired entries performs zero run-object GETs and PUTs.
A GC rebuild reconstructs cursors and edges but reclaims nothing; blobs not named by a surviving manifest are retained as `unaccounted`.
A reclaim test must advance the ack between rounds because the deletion pipeline is condemn at K, `delete_pending` at K+1, and physical delete at K+2 when all acks are current.
Part-manifest cleanup must remain edge-driven by in-degree rather than namespace-prefix ownership because shadow snapshots can reference manifests under dropped table prefixes.
A blob is live if a live manifest names it, and a manifest is live if a committed or precommitted ref names it.
CAS has exactly one blob-body deletion site: the pre-CAS `pending_deletes` phase of a GC round, limited to entries marked `delete_pending` by a previously published round.
GC never invents a ref transition; abandoned precommit cleanup is performed by the writer or its successor rather than by a synthetic GC event.
The GC condemnation marker is add-only: GC may change `Clean` to `Condemned` and delete the marker after a confirmed body delete, but never changes `Condemned` back to `Clean`.
A blob `.meta` sidecar has only `Clean` and `Condemned` states; an absent sidecar reads as `Clean`, and the sidecar contains no token.
A pre-precommit orphan manifest has no ref-log owner edge and is reclaimed by the orphan sweep, whereas a dangling precommit must first have its binding removed before GC can reclaim the body.
Blob liveness is represented by a set of source edges; `precommitAdd` creates `+1` edges, owner removals create `-1` edges, `promote` creates no edge, and inline manifest entries create none.
GC discovers the ref live set by listing `cas/ns/stream/`, joining opaque life ids to one catalog cut, and folding each admitted log only after its complete coverage is durable.
The implemented GC round is a single pass of 18 named phases ending in exactly one `gc/state` CAS; the older `fold → retire → fence → recheck → trim` shape is superseded.

`gc/state` is the durable round-adoption state and exactly one CAS per round publishes it; the fold seal records generation, parent generation, catalog-life coverage, source-edge runs, and condemned summaries.
Condemned entries are stored as sentinel rows in the source-edge run; there is no separate retired-list object and no run-file list outside the fold seal.

A blob candidate is HEAD-observed with an exact token when its edge set becomes empty; a carried candidate pays no HEAD, and missing bodies are non-throwing while present-but-invalid bodies are `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A condemned entry graduates only after surviving the required round delay and confirmed `Condemned` evidence for the exact `(hash, token)`; recovery spares it, and a token mismatch leaves the newer blob untouched.

The GC coordinator owns discovery, round visibility, the global fence, and generation advancement; reducers own disjoint digest shards, and pure-carry shards copy parent run references with zero run I/O.

The planned incarnation-aware fold treats a sealed/live incarnation mismatch as an absent prior cursor, restarts at `folded_cursor = 0`, drops carried edges from the old incarnation, and stamps the live incarnation into the new seal.
The planned ref-shard reclaim condition is empty refs, a last journal tombstone, complete folding past the fence at the current incarnation, and token-guarded `deleteExact`.

Before D1, `discoverUniverse` enumerated `registry.namespaces × shardsToVisit`, so GC fencing cost was proportional to namespaces ever created times `root_shards` and could mint fence-only manifests for absent shards.
The D1 fold cursor is keyed by `(ns, shard, incarnation)`, so a recreated shard with a strictly greater incarnation cannot match an old sealed cursor and is folded from zero.
An abandoned newborn is treated as an abandoned precommit and reclaimed by the existing `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` watermark path; after it empties, tombstone reclaim handles its shard object.

Successful copy-forward emits `CasEventType::BlobCopyForward` and increments `CasBlobCopyForward`; the old `(hash, t)` entry remains listed until exact-token settlement, while the new incarnation is protected from wrong-token deletion.

An ack-floor entry graduates only when `condemn_round < min_ack`, where `min_ack` is the minimum `observed_gc_round` among live or expired-but-not-fenced heartbeats; terminated and fenced heartbeats are excluded.

The ack-floor open ordering is claim heartbeat → load `gc/state` and the retired list → stamp the acknowledgement → enable mutations, and retired-list objects must be durable before the `gc/state` CAS publishes the round.

The three-cursor merge graduates entries with `condemn_round < min_ack`, keeps entries at `condemn_round == min_ack`, spares entries whose in-degree recovers, captures a token for new zero-in-degree condemnations, and skips absent blobs.

The current retired-candidate set is stored as per-GC-shard artifacts using the strict `cas_retired_set` protobuf codec (`RetiredSetProto`, magic `CART`), with entries sorted by `(kind, hash)` and each entry containing `(blob_hash, token, condemn_round)`.

The retired-list and `condemn_round` protobuf fields are additive fields in the same compatibility regime as `snap_attempt`; no per-object version integer is bumped, and future `compatibility_version` values fail closed.
GC computes `min_ack` as the minimum `observed_gc_round` among live heartbeats; terminated heartbeats are excluded, and if no live heartbeats exist then `min_ack = +∞`.

Discovery performs one paginated LIST of `cas/refs/` and ETag-diffs it against per-shard folded tokens; backends with `supportsListTokens = false` use per-shard HEAD/GET and remain fail-closed and read-only.

The GC merge processes the prior snapshot run, sorted edge deltas, and prior retired run with three cursors sorted by `blob_hash`, emitting the new snapshot run, retired run, and delete list in one streaming pass.
A retired candidate with recovered in-degree greater than zero is spared and removed from the retired output; the implementation emits a B170 recheck-verdict event with the recovered in-degree.
A retired candidate with zero in-degree graduates only when `condemn_round < min_ack`; a zero-in-degree candidate with `condemn_round >= min_ack` remains in the retired list.
